record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: Find a probabilistic operation X on an i.i.d. sequence (a_1,a_2,...) that plays a role for random-matrix statistics analogous to summation in the classical central limit theorem: after applying X to the first n inputs, the resulting random variables should converge, as n→∞, to the Gaudin distribution or to a Tracy-Widom distribution. In other words, characterize random-matrix universality in purely probabilistic terms.

evidence.quote: The question is, "What is X?" Important progress towards answering this question has been made recently, and independently, by Baik-Suidan and Bodineau-Martin, but the full problem remains open and very challenging.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The classical central limit theorem can be cast as follows: there is a probabilistic operation, namely normalized summation S_n(a_1,...,a_n) = (a_1+...+a_n - n μ)/(σ √n), such that for any i.i.d. sequence (a_i) with mean μ and finite variance σ^2, the law of S_n converges as n→∞ to the standard Gaussian distribution. The Gaussian distribution is therefore a universal attractor under the operation of summation.

In random matrix theory, two distributions play a comparably universal role for spectral statistics: 
(i) the Gaudin (sine-kernel gap) distribution, describing the limiting spacing between consecutive eigenvalues in the bulk of large Hermitian random matrices; 
(ii) the Tracy–Widom distributions F_β (β = 1, 2, 4), describing the limiting fluctuations, after appropriate centering and scaling, of the largest eigenvalue of large random matrices from the classical β-ensembles. Equivalently, F_2 is the limit law of the rescaled length of the longest increasing subsequence of a uniformly random permutation, and of various last-passage percolation times.

Problem. Exhibit a probabilistic operation X — that is, for each n, a measurable map X_n : R^n → R (or into a suitable state space) — with the following property:
For every i.i.d. sequence (a_1, a_2, ...) of real-valued random variables in some natural class (e.g. with sufficiently many finite moments, possibly normalized), the random variable X_n(a_1,...,a_n), after deterministic centering and scaling, converges in distribution as n→∞ to:
- the Gaudin (sine-kernel) distribution, or
- a Tracy–Widom distribution F_β for some β ∈ {1,2,4}.

The operation X should be intrinsically probabilistic (not requiring as input a random matrix model or an integrable structure), and should make the universality of Tracy–Widom / Gaudin laws as transparent as the role of summation in the classical CLT. In short, characterize random-matrix universality in purely probabilistic terms by identifying such an operation X.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally still considered open, but partial progress exists. Baik–Suidan (2005) and independently Bodineau–Martin proved a GUE central limit theorem implying Tracy–Widom universality for last-passage percolation in thin rectangles, by coupling random walks to Brownian motion via Tusnády-type approximations. Subsequent work has extended such universality results, but no fully general probabilistic operation X playing the role of summation in the classical CLT — yielding Tracy–Widom or Gaudin limits for arbitrary i.i.d. inputs — has been identified.

status_evidence.title: A GUE Central Limit Theorem and Universality of Directed First and Last Passage Site Percolation
status_evidence.snippet: Baik and Suidan prove a GUE central limit theorem for random variables with finite fourth moment, and apply it to obtain Tracy-Widom universality for directed last passage percolation in thin rectangles.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on identifying a probabilistic operation yielding Tracy-Widom limits, restricted to thin-rectangle regimes.

status_evidence.title: At the Far Ends of a New Universal Law
status_evidence.snippet: The Tracy-Widom distribution arises across many models, but a unified probabilistic explanation of its universality remains elusive.
status_evidence.claim: A general probabilistic characterization of Tracy-Widom universality is still sought.
